facts: Challenge in these appeals is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Patna High Court upholding the conviction of the appellants for offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short' IPC') so far as accused Ajeet Kumar Rai @ Ajeet Narayan Rai and Vinay Kumar Rai, appellant No.1 in Criminal appeal 371 of 2006 and Ashutosh Kumar Rai @ Sanjay Kumar Rai, appellant in other Criminal Appeal.
Ashutosh Kumar Rai was further charged for committing the murder of Nanda Kumar Singh punishable under Section 302 IPC and Section 27 of the Arms Act, 1959 (in short 'Arms Act').
The High Court dismissed the appeals.
The present appeals had been filed by Vinay Kumar Rai (A-3) and Ajeet Kumar Rai @ Ajeet Narayan Rai (A-1) and Ashutosh Kumar Rai (A-2).

The Presiding Officer, Additional Court No.1, Fast Track Court in Sessions Trial Nos. 578/96 and 1/2001 held Ajeet Kumar Rai and Vinay Kumar Rai guilty under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC and accused Ashutosh Kumar Rai under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for life.
He was also found guilty of offence under Section 27 of the Arms Act and sentenced to undergo RI for three years.
Two appeals were filed before the High Court which by the impugned judgment dismissed the same.

All accused were put on trial for committing the murder of Nanda Kumar Singh (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') in furtherance of their common intention for offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
issues: Whether the prosecution version should be accepted despite alleged discrepancy between medical evidence and oral evidence
Whether the eye-witnesses' testimony can be discarded due to their relationship with the deceased
petitioner_arguments: There was a discrepancy between the medical evidence and the oral evidence, which makes it difficult to accept the prosecution version.
The eye-witnesses are closely related to the deceased and therefore their testimony should not be relied upon.
respondent_arguments: The witnesses' testimony is cogent and credible, despite being family members of the deceased.
There was no attempt by the witnesses to intervene to save the life of the deceased, which suggests that they were telling the truth.
court_reasoning: A witness is normally considered independent unless there are sources that suggest otherwise.
Relationship between a witness and the victim does not necessarily mean that the witness's testimony should be discarded.
Each case must be judged on its own facts, rather than relying on general rules or assumptions.
holding: The appeals were dismissed, upholding the conviction of the appellants for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
